correctness.rationale: The q-round EF invariant is a partial bijection of the underlying points, preserving every chosen two-set. Before round j, at most 2(j-1) points on either side are assigned; if both root orders are at least 2q, the bijection can extend to the at most two new points, irrespective of Spoiler's side. Equality and intersection, hence the partial graph isomorphism, are preserved. For the path-forest lemma, in a path on s selected vertices each representing edge after the first meets its predecessor in one endpoint and is disjoint from all earlier edges other than that predecessor; it adds exactly one point. Distinct components use disjoint points, yielding the stated minimum, realized by disjoint root paths. An independent short check of the full lower bound is to take n=2k and use exactly one adjacency plus k-1 isolated selected vertices; the adjacent pair uses exactly three points and the isolates 2(k-1) fresh points, for minimum root order 2k+1. For n=2k+1, use k+1 pairwise disjoint two-sets, needing 2k+2 points. Both witnesses are existential of rank k+1, including n=2,3. They hold in every larger order and fail at n. Thus the formula separates exactly the claimed pairs and establishes the existential collapse, the least distinguishing rank, and the 2q-1 class count (empty singleton list at q=1). Bounded checks of these two pattern types for q=2,3,4,5 give respective first root orders 3,5,7,9 and 4,6,8,10. The frozen checker and its recorded q<=4 output were inspected, not executed or treated as an EF proof.
